title: Pensioners: a new 2027 form can protect resident-tax deductions
summary: Mula 2027 tax year, mas maraming pensioners ang padadalhan ng 扶養親族等申告書 kahit hindi sila subject sa pension income-tax withholding. If you qualify for spouse, dependent, disability or similar deductions, ignoring the form can mean higher resident tax unless you later correct it through a tax filing.
why_it_matters: The mailing threshold drops sharply for 2027 because the form now also carries resident-tax deduction information. A pensioner who previously assumed 'hindi ako kinakaltasan ng income tax, so wala akong kailangang form' can now miss deductions and create extra filing work.

claims.text: For 2027, Japan Pension Service will send the declaration to old-age/retirement pension recipients from annual pension amounts of ¥980,000 if under 65 and ¥1.48 million if 65 or older; the 2026 mailing thresholds were ¥1.55 million and ¥2.05 million respectively.
claims.basis: Current Japan Pension Service 2027 mailing table.

claims.text: The expanded mailing exists because pensioners who may owe resident tax can now use this integrated form to claim spouse, dependent and other deductions even when their pension is not subject to income-tax withholding.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service and NTA describe the form as serving both pension withholding and individual resident-tax declarations.

claims.text: Japan Pension Service says that if a person who qualifies for deductions does not submit the form and does not later make the necessary tax filing, applicable deductions such as disability or spouse deductions will not be reflected and more income tax or resident tax may be collected.
The highest-risk group is pensioners newly pulled into the mailing range who are used to discarding this document because they previously had no pension income-tax withholding.
claims.basis: The threshold expansion creates a new recipient group, while non-filing can leave deductions unapplied.

content.key_message: Kung may dumating na 令和9年分 扶養親族等申告書 this September, huwag i-assume na irrelevant dahil walang income-tax withholding sa pension mo.
what_changed: The 2027 form starts mailing from September 7, 2026.
The sending threshold falls to ¥980,000/year for pensioners under 65 and ¥1.48 million/year for those 65+, versus ¥1.55 million and ¥2.05 million for the 2026 form.
The reason is a real scope change: the form now also targets people who may need resident-tax deductions, not only pensioners subject to income-tax withholding.
content.who_is_affected: Primarily recipients of old-age or retirement pensions who meet the new mailing threshold and who themselves qualify as disabled, widow/single parent, or have a spouse/dependent or other qualifying family relationship that can generate tax deductions. People with no applicable deductions generally do not gain by submitting solely because the form arrived.
content.when: Japan Pension Service says paper forms for 2027 will be sent sequentially from September 7, 2026. Follow the deadline printed on your own form; the official guidance does not give one single nationwide return date for every recipient.
content.financial_impact: Varies by deduction, municipality and taxable income. No universal yen saving can be stated safely. The official consequence is that qualifying deductions may not be reflected, which can cause higher resident tax and/or income tax until corrected.
content.risk_if_ignored: If you qualify for a deduction and neither submit the pension declaration nor later file the appropriate tax return/declaration, Japan Pension Service says the deduction will not be applied and more tax may be collected.
content.deadline: Use the individual deadline printed on the 2027 declaration when it arrives; mailing begins September 7, 2026.
content.potential_benefit: Avoid missing spouse/dependent/disability-related deductions and avoid an unnecessary later correction or tax filing.
content.downside: Not everyone who receives the form needs to submit it. The nationwide mailing threshold is deliberately broad because resident-tax non-taxable limits vary by municipality.
content.common_mistake: Thinking 'no income tax is withheld from my pension, so this form cannot matter.' From the 2027 form onward, that assumption is no longer safe because resident-tax deductions are part of the scope.

fact_vs_inference.fact: The threshold expansion, September 7 mailing start, integrated resident-tax purpose and non-filing consequence are stated by Japan Pension Service/NTA.
fact_vs_inference.inference: Newly included pensioners are more likely to overlook the letter because they were outside the prior withholding-focused workflow.

content.strongest_counterinterpretation: Missing the form does not necessarily mean the deduction is permanently lost. The official FAQ says the problem applies if you also do not make the necessary later tax filing. So this is best understood as a simpler front-door procedure that prevents higher withholding/resident-tax assessment and extra correction work, not a one-chance-only benefit.
content.what_remains_uncertain: The actual resident-tax saving depends on the person's deduction eligibility, other income and municipality. Also, the mailing threshold uses the lowest resident-tax non-taxable threshold nationwide, so receiving a form does not itself prove that a person owes resident tax or must submit it.
content.what_would_change_mind: If Japan Pension Service withdraws or materially changes the September 7 mailing guidance, or issues new instructions making the expanded resident-tax declaration automatic without recipient action, ALAM should revise the action recommendation.

reading_levels.30 sec: What happened: mas maraming pensioners ang makakatanggap ng 2027扶養親族等申告書 starting Sept. 7. Why it matters: kahit walang pension income-tax withholding, puwedeng kailangan ito para ma-reflect ang resident-tax deductions. What to do: basahin ang form and submit if you have applicable spouse/dependent/disability etc. deductions. Bottom line: huwag basta itapon dahil lang 'wala naman akong income tax.'
reading_levels.2 min: For the 2027 declaration, Japan Pension Service lowered the mailing threshold to ¥980,000 annual pension for under-65s and ¥1.48 million for age 65+, because the same form now also carries information used for resident-tax deductions. If you have qualifying deductions, non-submission plus no later tax filing can leave them unapplied and increase tax collected. But receiving the form does not automatically mean you owe tax or must submit; the nationwide sending threshold is broad because municipal resident-tax thresholds vary.

outcomes: Understand why a pensioner with no income-tax withholding may suddenly receive this form.
Know when the form matters and when it can be ignored.
learning.background: Until now, many pensioners associated the 扶養親族等申告書 mainly with income tax withheld from pension payments. The 2026 tax reform expanded the 2027 form's role so resident-tax deductions can also be captured through Japan Pension Service. That means the mailing population becomes much larger.

terms.meaning: A pension-recipient declaration used to report spouse, dependent, disability and related deduction information.
terms.why_it_matters: From the 2027 form, it also serves more pensioners who may need those deductions reflected in resident tax.

terms.meaning: Local individual resident tax charged by prefectures and municipalities based mainly on the previous year's income and deductions.
terms.why_it_matters: A person may owe or need to calculate resident tax even when no national income tax is withheld from their pension.

how_it_works.title: Why the threshold suddenly fell
how_it_works.explanation: Japan Pension Service now sends the form not only to pensioners in the national income-tax withholding range but also to people who may enter the resident-tax range. Because resident-tax non-taxable limits vary by municipality, the nationwide sending threshold uses a conservative low cutoff.

how_it_works.title: What happens if you have deductions
how_it_works.explanation: The pensioner reports qualifying spouse/dependent/disability information. Japan Pension Service uses the form for pension tax processing and supplies relevant information for resident-tax calculation. If the form is skipped, the deduction can still potentially be corrected through later tax filing, but it is no longer automatic.

learning.example: Example: a 68-year-old receiving ¥1.6 million/year in old-age pension would have been below the ¥2.05 million 2026 form threshold, but is above the ¥1.48 million 2027 mailing threshold. If that person has an eligible spouse or disability deduction, the new form can matter even though the pension amount alone may not trigger national income-tax withholding.
takeaways: The 2027 mailing population is much wider than 2026.
No pension income-tax withholding does not automatically mean 'no form needed.'
Only people with applicable deductions need the form for those deductions.
Receiving the form does not by itself prove you owe resident tax.
If you miss it, later tax filing may still fix the issue, but that creates extra work.

action_plan.goal: Make sure any pension-related spouse, dependent, disability or similar deductions are reflected without needing a later correction.
action_plan.who_should_act: Act if you receive the 令和9年分 form and you have an applicable deduction or are unsure. If you have no applicable deductions, official guidance says submission is generally unnecessary.
action_plan.deadline: Use the return deadline printed on your own form; Japan Pension Service begins sending the 2027 form September 7, 2026.
prepare: The 令和9年分扶養親族等申告書 or electronic notice from Japan Pension Service.
Information for any spouse/dependent or personal disability/widow/single-parent status you intend to claim.
My Number Portal / Nenkin Net access if you prefer electronic submission.

steps.step: Check whether you actually need to file
steps.action: Use the Japan Pension Service guidance to see whether you have any applicable deduction.
steps.how: Review the eligibility section on the official 扶養親族等申告書 page or the decision guidance included with the notice.
steps.done_when: You can clearly say either 'I have an applicable deduction' or 'I have none.'

steps.step: Submit through the official route if needed
steps.action: Complete the declaration by paper or electronically.
steps.how: Paper recipients can follow the enclosed Japan Pension Service instructions; My Number Portal users linked to Nenkin Net can use the official electronic application.
steps.done_when: Electronic submission shows completion or the paper form has been sent according to the enclosed instructions.

steps.action: Keep your submitted copy/confirmation and later verify tax documents.
steps.how: Retain the electronic completion record or a copy/photo of the paper form and check your subsequent pension withholding/resident-tax documents.
steps.done_when: You have a retrievable record of what you declared.

mistakes_to_avoid: Throwing the form away solely because no income tax is withheld from your pension.
Assuming everyone who receives the form must submit it.
Assuming ¥1.48 million is a universal resident-tax taxable threshold; local non-taxable limits vary.
Using a non-official website or message to submit My Number or pension information.

decision_rules.if: You receive the form and have a spouse/dependent/disability or other listed deduction
decision_rules.then: Submit by the deadline printed on your form.

decision_rules.if: You receive the form but have no applicable deductions
decision_rules.then: Official guidance says submission is generally unnecessary.

decision_rules.if: You miss the form deadline or already discarded it
decision_rules.then: Do not assume the deduction is permanently lost; check Japan Pension Service and, if necessary, the appropriate later tax filing route.

action_plan.follow_up: Re-check your tax treatment when 2027 pension withholding documents and the following resident-tax assessment become available. If the deduction is absent, use the official tax/municipal correction route.
